question: A child with lymphoma and a large anterior mediastinal mass may develop superior vena cava syndrome and respiratory compromise under general anaesthesia, making biopsy under local anaesthesia preferable to general anaesthesia when feasible.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Anterior mediastinal masses in lymphoma compress the trachea and SVC. Under GA (supine + muscle paralysis), respiratory collapse and haemodynamic compromise are life-threatening risks. When a tissue diagnosis is needed, local anaesthesia in the sitting position or biopsy from a peripheral node is preferred.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The anterior mediastinal mass compresses the trachea and SVC in the supine position. Under general anaesthesia, muscle relaxation eliminates the spontaneous respiratory effort that maintains airway patency, and the supine position worsens SVC compression — risks include cardiovascular collapse and airway obstruction. Local anaesthesia with the child sitting upright is safer.
